say.en: Two batsmen both average 50. One scores 48, 50 and 52; the other scores 0, 50 and 100. Whom would you pick for a steady innings? In this lesson: Explain what dispersion means.
Tell absolute measures from relative measures.
Find the range and coefficient of range.

body.en: *Dispersion* is the scatter or spread of the values about a central value. An average alone does not describe the data; a measure of dispersion tells how far the values lie from it. Absolute measures (range, quartile deviation, mean deviation, standard deviation) are in the units of the data. Relative measures (coefficients) are pure numbers, so they can compare series in different units.
body.kn: ಚದುರಿಕೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಬೆಲೆಯ ಸುತ್ತ ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ಹರಡುವಿಕೆ. ನಿರಪೇಕ್ಷ ಅಳತೆಗಳು ದತ್ತಾಂಶದ ಏಕಮಾನದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತವೆ; ಸಾಪೇಕ್ಷ ಅಳತೆಗಳು (ಗುಣಾಂಕಗಳು) ಏಕಮಾನರಹಿತ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಬೇರೆ ಏಕಮಾನಗಳ ಶ್ರೇಣಿಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸಬಹುದು.

body.en: *Range* $R = H - L$, where H and L are the largest and smallest values. For a continuous distribution, H is the upper limit of the highest class and L the lower limit of the lowest class. Coefficient of range $= (H - L)/(H + L)$. Range is quick and easy, used in quality control and weather reports, but it depends only on the two extreme values.
body.kn: ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ R = H − L; H ಗರಿಷ್ಠ, L ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಬೆಲೆ. ನಿರಂತರ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ H ಮೇಲಿನ ವರ್ಗದ ಮೇಲ್ಮಿತಿ, L ಕೆಳಗಿನ ವರ್ಗದ ಕೆಳಮಿತಿ. ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಯ ಗುಣಾಂಕ = (H − L)/(H + L). ಇದು ಸುಲಭ, ಆದರೆ ಎರಡು ತೀವ್ರ ಬೆಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Find the range and the coefficient of range of the marks 32, 45, 28, 50, 41, 36.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Find the range and the coefficient of range of the marks 32, 45, 28, 50, 41, 36.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Find the range and the coefficient of range of the marks 32, 45, 28, 50, 41, 36.
H equals 50 and L equals 28.
Range equals 50 minus 28 equals 22 marks.
Coefficient of range equals 22 over 50 plus 28 equals 22 over 78 equals 0.2821.
So the answer is Range equals 22 marks; coefficient equals 0.28.

problem.en: Weekly wages (₹ hundreds) are grouped as 10–20, 20–30, 30–40, 40–50 and 50–60. Find the range and its coefficient.

steps.en: H = upper limit of the highest class = 60; L = lower limit of the lowest class = 10.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Weekly wages (₹ hundreds) are grouped as 10–20, 20–30, 30–40, 40–50 and 50–60. Find the range and its coefficient.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Weekly wages (₹ hundreds) are grouped as 10-20, 20-30, 30-40, 40-50 and 50-60. Find the range and its coefficient.
H equals upper limit of the highest class equals 60; L equals lower limit of the lowest class equals 10.
Range equals 60 minus 10 equals 50.
Coefficient equals 50 over 70 equals 0.714.
So the answer is Range equals 50 (₹ hundreds); coefficient equals 0.71.
